newsitem.title: USA: ISS opposes CPT's West Virginia proposal.
newsitem.headline: ISS opposes CPT's West Virginia proposal.

text.p: Institutional Shareholders Services have recommended that shareholders of Steel of West Virgina Inc vote against a proposal to have the board of directors negotiate the sale of the company, West Virginia said Tuesday.
ISS recommended to its subscribers that the holders vote against a proposal made by CPT Holdings Inc CPTH.O to have the board negotiate with potential bidders including CPT, it said.

On May 5, CPT said it had begun soliciting proxies from the holders for use at West Virginia's annual meeting. It said it was also asking them to vote against an increase in authorized common stock, an authorization of preferred stock and the elimination of the holders' right to act by written consent.
West Virginia cited the ISS as saying that it was satisfied with the board's plan to enhance shareholder value like expanding into the manufactured housing market.

"The company's results for the first quarter of 1997, which are a drastic improvement over the results for the same period in 1996, in addition to the improving stock price, lead us to believe that management has the company on the right track," it said.
West Virginia said the CPT proposal was "poorly timed, grossly inadequate, and not in the best interest of our stockholders."
